A_5_1.title: Policies for Information Security
A_5_1.description: The company writes its security rules down, in one overall policy and shorter ones on single topics such as passwords or remote work, and makes sure the people they apply to have read them. Recommendation: management approves them, and they are reviewed once a year.

A_5_2.title: Information Security Roles and Responsibilities
A_5_2.description: Each security task has a named owner, from the person running the ISMS to the owners of systems and information, and everyone knows who is responsible for what.

A_5_3.title: Segregation of Duties
A_5_3.description: Tasks that would let one person cause and hide a mistake or misuse, such as ordering and approving a payment or granting and using an access right, are split between different people.

A_5_4.title: Management Responsibilities
A_5_4.description: Managers expect their teams to follow the security rules and set the example themselves.

A_5_5.title: Contact with Authorities
A_5_5.description: The company knows which authorities to contact and when, such as the data protection authority, its CSIRT or competent authority and the police, and keeps their contact details current.

A_5_6.title: Contact with Special Interest Groups
A_5_6.description: Staff with security tasks keep in touch with outside groups that share security knowledge, such as industry associations, warning services or regional security networks.

A_5_7.title: Threat Intelligence
A_5_7.description: The company gathers information about threats that concern it, for example warnings from authorities and vendors, and adjusts its measures to it.

A_5_8.title: Information Security in Project Management
A_5_8.description: Security is part of every project from the start: risks are considered when the project is planned and checked before its results go live.

A_5_9.title: Inventory of Information and Other Associated Assets
A_5_9.description: The company keeps a list of its information and of the systems, devices and services that hold it, each with an owner, and keeps the list current.

A_5_10.title: Acceptable Use of Information and Other Associated Assets
A_5_10.description: Written rules say how staff may use company information and devices, for example private use of laptops, where files are stored or the use of public Wi-Fi.

A_5_11.title: Return of Assets
A_5_11.description: When someone leaves or changes role, they hand back the devices, keys, documents and other company property they hold.

A_5_12.title: Classification of Information
A_5_12.description: Information is sorted into a few protection levels, for example public, internal and confidential, so that everyone knows how carefully to handle it.

A_5_13.title: Labelling of Information
A_5_13.description: Information is labelled following the company's classification scheme, so everyone handling it sees how it is to be protected. Recommendation: a visible mark on documents, metadata on files.

A_5_14.title: Information Transfer
A_5_14.description: Rules cover how information may be passed on, by email, file transfer, messenger, on paper or in conversation, and agreements cover transfers to outside parties.

A_5_15.title: Access Control
A_5_15.description: Rules say who may access which information and systems, based on what each person needs for their work and no more.

A_5_16.title: Identity Management
A_5_16.description: Identities of people and systems are managed through their whole life: created, changed and removed through a controlled process. Recommendation: one identity per account, so every action can be traced to someone.

A_5_17.title: Authentication Information
A_5_17.description: Passwords, keys and tokens are handed out, stored and changed through a controlled process, and users know how to keep them secret.

A_5_18.title: Access Rights
A_5_18.description: Access rights are granted, changed and removed according to the access rules and checked regularly. Recommendation: check them every quarter.

A_5_19.title: Information Security in Supplier Relationships
A_5_19.description: The company identifies the risks that come with each supplier, above all those with access to its information or systems, and decides how to handle them.

A_5_20.title: Addressing Information Security Within Supplier Agreements
A_5_20.description: Contracts with suppliers who handle company information state the security requirements they have to meet.

A_5_21.title: Managing Information Security in the ICT Supply Chain
A_5_21.description: For IT products and services it buys, the company also looks at the security of its suppliers' own suppliers, for example through component lists or by passing its requirements on along the chain.

A_5_22.title: Monitoring, Review and Change Management of Supplier Services
A_5_22.description: The company checks regularly whether suppliers deliver the agreed security, and handles changes to their services in a controlled way.

A_5_23.title: Information Security for Use of Cloud Services
A_5_23.description: Before using a cloud service the company sets its security requirements, and it plans how to manage the service and how to leave it, including getting its data back.

A_5_24.title: Information Security Incident Management Planning and Preparation
A_5_24.description: The company prepares for incidents before they happen: who does what, how incidents are reported and escalated, and whom to inform.

A_5_25.title: Assessment and Decision on Information Security Events
A_5_25.description: Reported security events are assessed against agreed criteria to decide whether they count as incidents.

A_5_26.title: Response to Information Security Incidents
A_5_26.description: Incidents are handled along the prepared procedure: contain them, remove the cause, recover, and record what was done.

A_5_27.title: Learning from Information Security Incidents
A_5_27.description: After an incident the company reviews what happened and uses the findings to improve its measures.

A_5_28.title: Collection of Evidence
A_5_28.description: When an incident may lead to legal steps, the company secures evidence in a way that keeps it usable, for example logs and copies of affected systems.

A_5_29.title: Information Security During Disruption
A_5_29.description: Plans for disruptions and emergencies keep security in place while the company runs in emergency mode.

A_5_30.title: ICT Readiness for Business Continuity
A_5_30.description: The IT systems that critical business processes depend on can be restored within the time the business needs, and this is tested.

A_5_31.title: Legal, Statutory, Regulatory and Contractual Requirements
A_5_31.description: The company lists the laws, regulations and contracts that set security requirements for it, and keeps the list current.

A_5_32.title: Intellectual Property Rights
A_5_32.description: The company respects other people's rights in software and content, for example by tracking its software licences, and protects its own.

A_5_33.title: Protection of Records
A_5_33.description: Records the company has to keep, such as accounting and contract records, are protected against loss, tampering and unauthorised access for as long as they must be kept.

A_5_34.title: Privacy and Protection of PII
A_5_34.description: The company knows which data protection laws apply to the personal data it handles, such as the GDPR, and meets their requirements.

A_5_35.title: Independent Review of Information Security
A_5_35.description: Someone independent of the people who run security, internal or external, reviews how the company manages information security from time to time and after major changes.

A_5_36.title: Compliance with Policies, Rules and Standards for Information Security
A_5_36.description: The company checks whether its security rules are actually followed, and records the results. Recommendation: managers check their teams, the security team checks across the company.

A_5_37.title: Documented Operating Procedures
A_5_37.description: Procedures for running IT, such as starting systems, backups or handling faults, are written down and available to the staff who need them.
